review_findings.retained_connections: Each retained connection has a particular narrated, verbal, legal, symbolic or commemorative basis. Same-chapter links concern instructions and fulfillment, reversal, explanation or explicit recap, and all 22 are labelled.
review_findings.composite_units: Both chapter-5 composites remain exact single units with all three continuation paragraphs each. There is no invented standalone 5:1 or 5:2.
review_findings.dates_and_source_wording: Nisa remains the first month; the thirteenth/fourteenth Adar differences remain visible. Slavery in 7:4 is not inserted into earlier letters. Bougaean and Macedonian, Artaxerxes, Aminadab, Zosara, fifteen thousand, Phrourai and against-health wording are preserved.
review_findings.textual_tensions: The reward notices, household-versus-sons sequence and distinct plunder accounts are compared without a fabricated harmonization. The 6:3-to-1:1q connection is an explicit textual contrast only; it does not resolve the separate zero-credit reward-chronology candidate in the Esther 1-4 packet.
review_findings.speaker_and_identity_limits: The royal letters' claims about the king's innocence and Haman's wider scheme remain attributed allegations. The narrator's Haman-entreaty description is kept distinct from the king's assault accusation. Bougathan/Gabatha and the possible 9:31 fasting connection remain unresolved and zero credit.
review_findings.external_comparisons: Courtly angel language, the half-kingdom offer, royal regalia and delegated authority are compared without conflating rulers or offices. The Daniel decree is not expanded to wording absent from its target. The seventh-month observance in Nehemiah and the distinct Adar commemorations are not merged.
review_findings.self_refinements: Exact history establishes only two rationale refinements: the third-day phrasing and the distinction concerning slavery. All 123 other original tuples are unchanged, and both corrected full triples were personally reread. No peer correction is required.

The attendants identify Haman in the court and the king summons him; this transition has no additional distinctive connection beyond the execution-request scene already retained.
The unfinished introduction to the honored man is completed in the following proposal; no independent target is selected for the introductory fragment.
The question asking who dared the deed introduces the identification of Haman; the question alone does not supply a further substantive comparison.
This unit only introduces the copy of the letter; the letter heading and particular provisions are reviewed in their own actual source units.
The general reflection on ingratitude and imagined escape from divine justice has no separately selected particular target beyond generic moral resemblance.
The accusation that Haman intended to transfer Persian rule to Macedonians is the letter's particular allegation; no independent narrative confirmation or external identity is established for it.
The precise sanction of spear, fire and permanent desolation for noncomplying regions is not linked to unrelated destruction or curse passages merely because their imagery overlaps.
Pharsannestain, Delphon and Phasga are preserved as names in the sons list; no individually distinguishing cross-text identities have been established.
Phardatha, Barea and Sarbacha are preserved as actual names in the sons list; no independent person-level comparison has been established.
Marmasima, Arouphaion, Arsaion and Zabouthaithan are not equated with other names or reconstructed forms without distinguishing evidence.
The delivery of the Susa casualty report is necessary context for the retained tally links; no additional substantive target is selected for the administrative transition itself.

The actual wording about establishing things against themselves and setting their plan against their own health is not silently replaced by a familiar fasting formulation; the separately read fasting proposal remains unresolved.
The land-and-sea tax notice supplies no specific amount, purpose or matched levy; a generic link to imperial taxation is insufficient.
The reference to the Persian and Median kings' memorial book does not identify a separately available passage in that record; generic royal wealth or annals formulas are insufficient.
The colophon's Dositheus, his son Ptolemy, translator Lysimachus and Ptolemy-Cleopatra dating are not assigned identities from common names or an unverified regnal reconstruction.
